comparator.name: Nutrition and Health
comparator.sourceNotes: Current2026–2027 BVG handbook:121EC compulsory common courses,3EC prior-mathematics-dependent choice and12EC literature thesis establish136EC of common study; this example uses44EC genuine electives to total180. The zero-to-four-credit optional skills group and6EC same-group laboratory thesis extension are not selected. All57B1 common credits plus3EC mathematics are completed; all60B2 compulsory credits and Skills Development Part1 precede thesis entry, exceeding the102compulsory-credit threshold. Part3 portfolio is completed with electives/thesis, not falsely required before it. General/laboratory safety are additional zero-credit requirements. No formal specialisation/minor instantiated; current module requirements and assessments control, not historical course guides.
components: Nutrition and Health: Macronutrients, Energy and Health
Both study carbohydrates, fats, proteins, enzymes and energy metabolism. WUR adds dedicated nutrition, body-weight regulation and the health effects of particular macronutrients.
Introduction to the Field of Nutrition and Health

WUR combines information-literacy training with Excel. UCR’s PPD shares scholarly searching and source evaluation, while adding writing, reflection and civic engagement; it does not reproduce the Excel module. General and laboratory safety are additional zero-credit requirements; laboratory safety must precede the practicals.

Both courses teach estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing. WUR also develops simple regression for life-science data; UCR’s Probability & Statistics has a more mathematical and computational emphasis.
General Chemistry for the Life Sciences

Shared chemical equilibria, thermodynamic and quantitative physical-chemical tools provide a partial relationship. UCR’s course uses sustainability and materials examples, rather than a full life-science chemistry sequence.

The shared microbiological methods include bacterial culture, identification and experimental analysis. WUR additionally studies microbial diversity and gastrointestinal microbiota; UCR’s laboratory course also covers blood, proteins and DNA.
Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
WUR teaches dietary-assessment instruments, reference values, biomarkers and measurement error. General interviewing or data analysis is not a substitute for this specialist training.
Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms for Health
Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health I

The shared research-design methods include questions, measurement, sampling, experimental planning and ethics. WUR applies these to nutritional protocols, including participant allocation, blinding and compliance.
Research Methodology for Nutrition and Health II

WUR students conduct a dietary intervention and measurements such as body composition, energy expenditure, biomarkers and sensory analysis. The selected UCR courses do not reproduce this integrated nutritional practical.
Skills development is an integrated portfolio of presenting, writing, collaboration and supporting skills. Part 1 must be completed before the thesis.
Part 3 develops and records presenting and writing through electives and the thesis. Its 1 EC is separate from the 12 EC thesis, rather than a duplicate thesis award.
This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for students with VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice is determined by prior preparation.

The required 12 EC thesis is an individual literature study with a research proposal, report, presentation and final discussion. Entry requires at least 102 credits of compulsory first- and second-year study, all first-year courses and Skills Development Part 1. The optional 6 EC laboratory extension is not selected here.
This example retains 44 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. Selecting optional skills courses or the laboratory thesis extension can reduce that space; neither is added here.

alternatives.label: Biomedical science, behaviour & public health
alternatives.labelReason: Study the biological mechanisms and behavioural determinants relevant to nutrition and health. Combine cellular biology, metabolism, human physiology and disease with epidemiology, health psychology and quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods.
alternatives.concept: Study the biological mechanisms and behavioural determinants relevant to nutrition and health. Combine cellular biology, metabolism, human physiology and disease with epidemiology, health psychology and quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods.
progression: Current formal prerequisites precede every dependent course; every assigned term is planned. Gateways precede disciplinary study, Cell Biology precedes Pathology/Genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, basic empirical design precedes research synthesis/advanced analysis, programming precedes ML and introductory sociology precedes modern sociology. These improvements do not create extra hard prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Molecular health, physiology & research methods
alternatives.labelReason: Investigate cellular, biochemical, physiological and genetic mechanisms of health and disease through laboratory work and quantitative research. Add anatomy, neurobiology, chemical foundations and research computing, while recognising the absence of a dedicated nutritional-science sequence.
alternatives.concept: Investigate cellular, biochemical, physiological and genetic mechanisms of health and disease through laboratory work and quantitative research. Add anatomy, neurobiology, chemical foundations and research computing, while recognising the absence of a dedicated nutritional-science sequence.
progression: Current formal prerequisites precede every dependent course; every assigned term is planned. Gateways precede disciplinary study, Cell Biology precedes Pathology/Genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, basic empirical design precedes research synthesis/advanced analysis, programming precedes ML and introductory sociology precedes modern sociology. These improvements do not create extra hard prerequisites.
alternatives.distinctness: The integrated response is reweighted toward molecular/organ mechanisms, anatomy, neurobiology, chemical tools and research computing rather than social/behavioural inquiry. Actual differences: 5 courses / 37.5 EC against programme1. These are concept-driven changes, not threshold swaps.

alternatives.label: Health behaviour, prevention & policy
alternatives.labelReason: Investigate how psychological, social and economic influences shape health behaviour and prevention. Combine epidemiology, physiology and health psychology with consumer decisions, health-policy appraisal, communication and empirical research methods.
alternatives.concept: Investigate how psychological, social and economic influences shape health behaviour and prevention. Combine epidemiology, physiology and health psychology with consumer decisions, health-policy appraisal, communication and empirical research methods.

Gateways precede disciplinary study, Cell Biology precedes Pathology/Genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, basic empirical design precedes research synthesis/advanced analysis, programming precedes ML and introductory sociology precedes modern sociology. These improvements do not create extra hard prerequisites.
alternatives.distinctness: The integrated response is reweighted toward health behaviour, consumer choice, inequalities, public economics and sugar-policy analysis rather than the molecular/laboratory sequence. Actual differences: 7 courses / 52.5 EC against programme1, 12 courses / 90 EC against programme2. These are concept-driven changes, not threshold swaps.

core: Human nutrition and health: dietary requirements, biological mechanisms and population effects
Cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics and biomedical disease mechanisms
Eating behaviour, social and psychological determinants and food choice
Statistics, dietary assessment, research design, data and individual literature research
adjacent: Molecular and experimental nutrition-related research, with optional biotechnology study
Optional data-science study and quantitative nutrition research
questions: How do nutrients and biological mechanisms affect human health and disease?
How can experiments, dietary measurements and literature synthesis test nutritional evidence?
How do social influences, food choices and prevention affect population health?

candidates.label: Quantitative nutrition research and optional data science
candidates.rationale: Current programme names Data Science as an optional minor. This separate organising direction is preserved as eligible evidence, not silently owned by the behavioural programme. Three coherent and distinct responses have already passed the sequential gates; a fourth programme is outside the maximum.

selection.assessment: Three coherent and substantively distinct related responses are implemented and feasible. Optional data-science direction remains separately owned after the maximum; the illustrated programmes are not a full nutritional-science curriculum.

trace: Direct cellular/molecular foundations, biomolecules, enzymes, energy metabolism, gene expression and scientific-paper analysis prepare investigation of nutritional mechanisms. The gateway does not establish hands-on laboratory training.

Neural signalling, learning, social influence and psychological/neuroscientific research appraisal provide specific foundations for later health-behaviour inquiry; not a dedicated eating-behaviour course.

Direct epidemiological measures/design, bias/confounding/causality, health promotion, screening and a needs-assessment/stakeholder project support population-health and prevention reasoning; the local health project is not guaranteed nutrition-specific.

Social boundaries, networks, stratification and inequality provide explanatory concepts for social and socioeconomic influences on health behaviour and access. The literature project is not itself a dietary study.

Direct measurement quality, sampling, survey/experimental designs, inference/regression and R-based empirical work support planning and evaluating health research. Nutritional intake instruments, blinding/compliance and metabolic measurements require additional specialist training.

Direct R cleaning, joining, exploration, visualisation and reproducibility support nutrition/health research-data analysis. No specific dietary dataset or algorithm/data-structures curriculum is guaranteed.

Direct social cognition, influence/persuasion, group processes and theory-guided research design help explain social determinants of health and food choice. The final study is proposed, not actually conducted.
Direct multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures designs, assumption checks and R analyses support rigorous human-health experiments and population evidence.

Direct digestive, endocrine, metabolic, cardiovascular and other organ-system regulation establishes physiological mechanisms through which diet can affect health. The literature paper does not replace dietary-intake or intervention practicals.

Direct protein/carbohydrate/lipid chemistry, enzyme kinetics, glycolysis, citric-acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and lipid/nitrogen metabolism supply a substantial macronutrient/energy mechanism core. Dedicated micronutrient requirements and dietary recommendations remain absent.

Persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and actual communication implementation supply tools for prevention messages and health-behaviour analysis. Current community projects concern sustainable/circular lifestyles, not a promised nutrition campaign.
Direct calculus, optimisation, differential equations and dynamic-model computation provide quantitative tools for biological rates and research modelling; no nutritional model project is guaranteed.

Direct membranes/bioenergetics, signalling, gene expression and cell regulation support cellular mechanisms underlying nutritional effects; the actual drug/cancer research context is not relabelled nutrigenomics.

Direct biochemical/microbial/molecular practicals include culture, blood analysis, protein purification, ELISA, transformation, DNA/PCR and bioinformatics. These are genuine experimental skills; body composition, food sensory panels and human dietary intervention methods remain different.

Moral argument, ethical theories and practical-dilemma reasoning support analysis of research participants, health claims and fair prevention choices. It is not a specialist research-regulation or food-law course.

Direct inheritance, variation, gene regulation/epigenetics, DNA technologies and cellular pathology support genetic/biomedical mechanisms and research planning. The grant proposal is not a nutrition trial; full nutritional genomics is not claimed.

Direct pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, toxicity and drug-response analysis address the pharmacological side of bioactive-compound evidence. Nutrient–drug interactions and food-supplement appraisal are more explicit at WUR.

Direct biopsychosocial determinants, health inequalities, prevention/behaviour-change models, chronic illness and health-interview practice support health behaviour and intervention appraisal; dietary counselling qualification and nutrient assessment are not claimed.

Direct probability, estimation/testing, confidence intervals, Bayesian reasoning and sampling/Monte Carlo methods support inferential uncertainty in health research; not the full applied nutrition regression/ANOVA course.

Direct innate/adaptive/mucosal immunity, host–microbe interactions and flow-cytometry/lymphocyte analysis supply substantial immunological and infection evidence. Gastrointestinal microbial ecology and nutritional immunomodulation are more specialist at WUR.

Direct digestive, cardiovascular, renal, endocrine and other disease mechanisms connect organ dysfunction to diagnosis, treatment and prognosis. These explain nutrition-related biological vulnerability without claiming a food-toxicology or diet-therapy curriculum.

Direct systematic searching, study selection, bias appraisal, effect-size extraction and fixed/random-effects meta-analysis in R implement rigorous evaluation of diet/health evidence as a specific transferable research method. The team synthesis project is not an individual12EC nutrition thesis or a guaranteed dietary-intervention study.

Direct interviews/focus groups, observation, coding and reflexivity supply qualitative tools for health experiences and food-choice contexts. General interviews do not substitute for nutritional-intake instruments or biomarkers.

Chemical equilibria, thermodynamic/energy principles and physical-chemical models supply a bounded complementary foundation for biomolecular processes. Its starch-biopolymer practical is actual experimental work, not food production or bio-organic reaction/stereochemistry training.

Direct Python collections, algorithms/structured problem solving, recursion, testing and debugging supply research-computing foundations. Health-domain exercises and specialist nutrition software are not promised.

Direct regression/classification, resampling/validation, regularisation and predictor evaluation in R/Python enable critical analysis of complex biomedical data. Prediction is not causal nutritional inference, and projects are not guaranteed nutrition datasets.

Actual abdominal, cardiovascular/respiratory and other anatomical structures, imaging and human-specimen interpretation deepen organ mechanisms supporting physiology and metabolic disease. This is anatomy rather than an additional nutrition course.

Actual neurobiological regulation, biological rhythms, lifestyle drugs and eating-disorder topics give a specific neural/behavioural perspective on bodily regulation and disrupted eating. It does not establish sensory panels, nutrient metabolism or the whole programme as neuroscience.
Consumer choice, incentives, production/costs and market models prepare analysis of food-choice constraints and public prevention policy; no specialist nutrition economics inferred.

Social construction, stigma/othering, social capital and intersectionality provide concrete theory for interpreting health inequalities and socially patterned behaviour; no dedicated food ethnography is guaranteed.

Persuasive appeals, arguments/fallacies, structured debate and speech delivery provide concrete tools for evaluating and presenting public health claims. The actual educational storytelling project concerns climate/community, not nutrition.

Direct efficiency/equity, public goods/externalities and public spending with explicit health/welfare/social-insurance applications provide a bounded health-policy appraisal method. It is not nutritional epidemiology.

Consumer choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences, cognitive limitations, market structure and regulation provide economic mechanisms for constrained food/health decisions. Actual algebraic/graphical theory and research appraisal support the behavioural concept.

The official description supports psychological biases, heuristics, framing, deviations from economic rationality and experiments. These are substantive decision tools for studying behaviour and prevention; no guaranteed food-choice experiment or undocumented nudge curriculum is claimed.

The official description explicitly uses a sugar case to analyse policy-making phases and national/international conceptualisations, with policy memos. This is a concrete nutrition-relevant policy-analysis contribution; no absent specialist public-health methods invented.
blocks: Shared cellular organisation, membranes, signalling, gene regulation and molecular methods; biological examples and practical scope differ.
Shared normal organ-system physiology, homeostasis, digestive/endocrine and energy regulation. WUR adds its own physiology practicals.

Shared carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, enzyme processes and energy metabolism are important primary content. WUR additionally develops macronutrient-specific nutrition/health effects and body-weight regulation.

Shared experimental microbial culture/identification, basic microbiology and biochemical/molecular laboratory reasoning. WUR additionally emphasises microbial diversity and gastrointestinal microbiota.
Shared inheritance, genetic variation, epigenetics, disease mechanisms and genetic technologies. WUR includes its own human-genetics wet-lab genotype/phenotype work.
Shared drug action, kinetics, metabolism and dose-response foundations. WUR additionally examines dietary bioactives, supplements and nutrient–drug interactions.
Shared innate/adaptive immunity, immune-cell mechanisms, immune disorders and laboratory-data analysis; WUR additionally examines nutritional immunomodulation.
Shared chemical equilibria, thermodynamic/energy and quantitative physical-chemical tools; UCR’s environmental/material contexts differ from the focused life-science chemistry course.
No adequate whole counterpart for organic reaction mechanisms, stereochemistry and natural-product chemistry; general biochemical/sustainability contributions remain bounded.
Distinct nutrition-specific orientation, longitudinal skills or assessment requirement is not equated with a generic method or broad introductory course.
Additional dedicated micronutrient/energy nutrition remains separate; the strongest biochemical macronutrient course is aligned to Macronutrients, Energy and Health.
No selected course directly implements food processing/storage effects on nutrient function/digestibility and food labelling/legislation.
Additional integrated normal physiological regulation/inter-organ training remains separate; the strongest shared physiological course is already aligned to Principles of Human Physiology.
Clinical disease mechanisms are not a substitute for toxicological exposure, organ-specific toxicity and risk assessment.
Dietary instruments, reference intakes, biomarkers and intake measurement error are not replaced by generic qualitative interviewing or data cleaning.
Additional human infectious-disease content remains separate; the strongest host-defence course is aligned to Human Immunology.
The integrated human dietary-intervention and nutritional-measurement practical is not reproduced by general laboratory or statistical training.
Shared epidemiological measures, designs, bias/confounding and population-health reasoning; UCR also develops intervention/stakeholder appraisal.
Shared social cognition, influence, group behaviour and theory-guided social-psychological research.
Shared biopsychosocial determinants of behaviour, health inequalities and prevention/behaviour-change frameworks. WUR focuses on eating patterns and nutritional behaviour.
Shared practical speech organisation, rhetorical choices, delivery and public presentation; UCR adds argumentation/storytelling and WUR targets scientific presentations.
No selected course implements food taste/smell panels, hedonic/analytical measures and food-product sensory profiling.
Research design, data, evidence synthesis & academic skills
Shared scholarly information searching, evaluation and academic research literacy. WUR additionally requires Excel; UCR adds writing, reflection and civic engagement.

Shared research-question/design, measurement, sampling, experimental logic, ethics and empirical project planning. WUR’s protocols are specifically nutritional, including blinding, allocation, compliance and participant measures.
Shared multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures designs, assumptions and R-based data interpretation.
Shared structured programming/problem solving, data collections and algorithmic implementation. WUR explicitly frames data structures and algorithms through health problems.
Shared functions, differentiation/integration and quantitative problem-solving support the selected conditional mathematics component. UCR extends into dynamic models and differential equations.
Shared probability-based estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. WUR develops simple applied regression; UCR emphasises mathematical inference and simulation.

Shared critical literature searching, evidence selection/appraisal and analytical synthesis/reporting give a specific research-method relationship. UCR has a taught team meta-analysis, while WUR requires an individual supervised12EC literature thesis with proposal, report, presentation and defence. Optional UCR research remains an additional opportunity.
Distinct nutrition-specific orientation, longitudinal skills or assessment requirement is not equated with a generic method or broad introductory course.

notes.text: WUR provides a dedicated nutrition sequence in macro- and micronutrients, food technology, dietary-intake measurement, food sensory science and human nutritional interventions. UCR can combine substantial biomedical mechanisms, physiology, epidemiology, health behaviour and research methods, but these related programmes do not reproduce that specialist sequence. WUR’s 12 EC individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Dutch-taught Nutrition and Health bachelor studies how diet and lifestyle affect human health, from molecules and organs to behaviour and populations. It combines biomedical science with nutritional assessment, food and sensory science, experiments and independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines biological mechanisms with health behaviour and public-health research. The second emphasises molecular and organ mechanisms, laboratory work and research computing; the third emphasises health behaviour, prevention and policy. These are related approaches: WUR offers substantially more dedicated nutritional science, dietary assessment, food technology, sensory testing and human nutrition interventions. Its individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
